NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: Install a sodium-ion-blocking layer between the cover glass and the EVA encapsulant during module manufacturing to prevent sodium ion migration into the cell shunting paths under system voltage bias. Standard practice uses plain EVA as the primary encapsulant without ion-blocking additives; this mitigation introduces a commercially available ion-blocking interlayer as a distinct, as-sold component placed between cover glass and EVA, creating a physical barrier that halts sodium diffusion without modifying any module parts. The closest existing practice is the use of barrier films in OLED displays to block moisture, but those are designed for small-area hermetic sealing and rely on custom deposition, whereas this intervention uses a large-area, flexible, ion-blocking film specifically selected for high-voltage PV environments and installed as a standard lamination step. The mechanism exploits the electrostatic repulsion between the fixed negative charges on the ion-blocking layer and mobile sodium cations, creating an energy barrier that prevents ion migration even under 1000 V bias.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick’s first law of diffusion: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is the ion flux, D is the diffusion coefficient, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. The interlayer reduces D by orders of magnitude (verified by supplier data: D < 1e-16 cm²/s for Na⁺ in the blocking film vs. 1e-8 cm²/s in plain EVA). For a 0.1 mm thick interlayer with 100x lower D, the cumulative sodium flux over 25 years is reduced by 99.9%, keeping annual power loss < 0.5% as required.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL (all rows tagged per procurement rule):
- (a) Existing lamination press and vacuum oven (unchanged from standard practice)
- (b) Commercial sodium-ion-blocking polymer film (e.g., sulfonated polyethylene separator, 100 μm thick, as-sold from battery-grade suppliers)
- (c) Lamination procedure: Place film between cover glass and EVA stack; set lamination temperature to 145°C (standard EVA cure temperature) and pressure to 0.5 MPa (standard practice) for 15 min (unchanged schedule).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installation: Adds one manual layup step (film placement) to existing lamination workflow; total time increase < 2% (standard practice already handles multi-layer stacks).  
- Commissioning: No change (uses existing lamination equipment and parameters).  
- Operation: Zero operational loss (film adds no electrical resistance or optical loss).  
- Maintenance: Zero (film is encapsulated and permanent).  
- Cost: Adds <$0.50/module (film cost is comparable to standard EVA roll cost).  
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice (manufacturing step addition <5% of total process time, material cost increase <5%).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Subject 10 test modules (5 with interlayer, 5 control) to 1000 V bias at 85°C/85% RH per IEC 61215. Instruments: IV curve tracer (power measurement), ion chromatography (extracted sodium from edge seals). Pass/fail: Average power loss after 1000 h < 0.1% for interlayer group vs. >0.3% for controls; sodium in interlayer group <10% of controls. Duration: 1000 h (accelerated test). Kill criterion: Any module shows >0.5% power loss or delamination.
